title: De mundanis apotelesmatibus excerptum ex libro Albumasaris
shelf_note: A Greek astrological manuscript; this leaf is a table of contents of astrological chapters (καταρχαί, Hermes, Julian of Laodicea, Heliodorus), consistent with the catalogue.
structure_note: The page is a recto with the stamped modern foliation '195', and the stored page-num is 195. 25 backsteps and 27 repeats are what you would expect from a mix of chapter numerals and foliation read as printed numbers. That points to an instrument artefact, not a scan splice.

title: Thucydides, Histories (MS, 11th c.)
shelf_note: Vat. gr. 126, Thucydides book 5 (5.46–47); matches the catalogue.
rights_flag: The scan carries a burned-in 'Copyright © Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana' banner and a diagonal 'Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana © ALL RIGHTS RESERVED' watermark. The work is medieval; the flag concerns the image licence, not the text.
structure_note: Large backstep and repeat counts in a manuscript usually reflect misread folio numerals. Nothing on this page suggests a splice.

title: Galeni Anatomicae aggressiones
shelf_note: The leaf holds pharmacological recipes (salves, honey, wine, frogs, mouse), not anatomy. Galenic manuscripts often bind several works together, so this does not show the catalogue is wrong; left as fits.
structure_note: 146 backsteps and 169 repeats out of 438 numbered pages is high. The stored page-num 44 matches a modern pencil '44' at the foot, but the red marginal recipe numerals (ρλγ…) are probably also being read as page numbers. That points to an instrument artefact, not a splice.

title: Bodleian Library MS. Canon. Gr. 110
shelf_note: The display title is 'The Epistle of Saint James', but this leaf is the opening of Philippians ('ΠΡΟΣ ΦΙΛΙΠΠΗΣΙΟΥΣ', Phil 1:1–2). The title may name only part of a 13-image Pauline/Catholic-epistles selection.
structure_note: This 13-page record is probably a selection of images from the manuscript, not the whole manuscript. The image is a close detail photograph, not a full leaf.
